author: Isabella Torregiani
title: Pentagon rushing to train thousands of National Guard troops for nationwide crackdown - NewsBreak
text:
By Isabella Torregiani ,
17 hours ago The Pentagon is racing to train more than 20,000 National Guard troops as a “quick reaction force” ready to respond to civil unrest. The move comes after anti-Trump demonstrations and the president’s own warnings that he might send “more than the National Guard” and use “dangerous cities as training grounds for our military National Guard.”
The report The documents reportedly outline a major expansion of President Donald Trump ’s proposal to deploy National Guard troops across U.S. cities. According to internal documents reviewed by The Washington Post , the Defense Department’s newly formed National Guard “quick reaction force” is required to be trained, fully equipped with riot-control gear and ready for deployment by January 1. The first 200 troops will be selected from Guard personnel who normally respond to emergencies such as nuclear accidents and terrorist attacks.
National Guard Reaction Force The National Guard is preparing for its largest nationwide deployment in years, with plans to expand by April, according to The Post . A separate but related unit, the National Guard Reaction Force, is expected to be fully operational by April 1. Once fully expanded, the combined force will total 23,500 troops across all 50 states and three territories, not including the District of Columbia. While most states will provide roughly 500 troops, others will contribute between 250 and 450. Traditionally reserved for emergencies like disaster relief, these forces are now being readied for civil unrest.
Political opponents Federal agencies and the military are increasingly being deployed against Trump’s political opponents. His Justice Department recently announced plans to send election monitors to polling sites in California. Voters in the state recently passed Proposition 50, a measure authorizing temporary changes to congressional district maps to boost Democratic-leaning districts in response to Texas’ mid‑decade partisan congressional redistricting. Top positions have also been filled by far-right election deniers. Now, with Pete Hegseth leading Pentagon operations, the National Guard may be ready to target the president’s critics.
‘Low morale’ Even some members of the National Guard are reportedly uneasy about Trump’s plans. Earlier this year, troops described “low morale and deep concern that the deployment may hurt recruitment,” according to The New York Times . More recently, two Illinois National Guard members told CBS News they would refuse orders to act against fellow residents in Chicago. They claimed the administration is exploiting public safety concerns to deploy the military against civilians.
